blocks.t: Some of the information in this section, including information with respect to our business plans and strategies, contain forwardlooking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. You should read the section titled “Forward-Looking Statements” on page 19 for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties related to those statements and also the sections titled “Risk Factors”, “Industry Overview”, “Financial Information” and “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” on pages 20, 150, 277 and 392, respectively, as well as financial and other information contained in this Red Herring Prospectus as a whole, for a discussion of certain factors that may affect our business, financial condition or results of operations. Our actual results may differ materially from those expressed in or implied by these forward-looking statements. Our Company was incorporated on June 5, 2023. Lohia Trade Services Limited (formerly known as Lohia Corp Limited) had filed a scheme of arrangement among our Company, Lohia Trade Services Limited (formerly known as Lohia Corp Limited) (the “Demerged Company”) and their respective shareholders and creditors, pursuant to which the Demerged Company’s technical textile machinery business undertaking which constituted its core business, including its investment in five subsidiaries, (together, the “Demerged Business”) was demerged and vested into our Company (such demerger scheme, the “Scheme”). The Scheme was approved by the National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench at Prayagraj (the “NCLT”) through its order dated April 16, 2024, with the appointed date of the Scheme being April 1, 2024 (the “Appointed Date”). The NCLT order sanctioning the Scheme was filed with the Registrar of Companies, Uttar Pradesh at Kanpur on May 1, 2024, being the effective date of the Scheme (the “Effective Date”). Pursuant to the Scheme, the name of our Company was changed from Kanpur Packaging Machines Limited to Lohia Corp Limited and the name of the Demerged Company was changed from Lohia Corp Limited to Lohia Trade Services Limited, which has subsequently been renamed to its present name, LTS Holdings Private Limited. For further information, see “History and Certain Corporate Matters – Details regarding material acquisitions or divestments of business/ undertakings, mergers, amalgamation, any revaluation of assets, etc. in the last 10 years.” on page 246. For comparative purposes, we have prepared Special Purpose Combined and Carve-Out Financial Statements for Fiscal 2024. The Special Purpose Combined and Carve-Out Financial Statements for Fiscal 2024 include the combined and carve-out financial statements in respect of the Demerged Business for the year ended March 31, 2024. The restated financial information for the period ended March 31, 2024 reflects the standalone financial information of our Company, as our Company had no operations since its incorporation on June 5, 2023 and prior to the Scheme being effective. The restated financial information for Fiscal 2024 reflects financial information for the period from June 5, 2023 (the date of our Company’s incorporation) to March 31, 2024. Consequently, the restated consolidated financial information for Fiscals 2026 and 2025 is not directly comparable to the restated standalone financial information for Fiscal 2024. The special purpose combined and carve-out financial statements for Fiscal 2024 included in this Red Herring Prospectus have been derived from the Special Purpose Combined and Carve-Out Financial Statements on page 350. Restated consolidated financial information for Fiscals 2026 and 2025 and restated standalone financial information for Fiscal 2024 included in this Red Herring Prospectus have been derived from the Restated Financial Information on page 277. …

We are among the leading global manufacturers of machinery and equipment for technical textiles in terms of revenue in 2024, with a strong focus on solutions for producing polypropylene (“PP”) and high-density polyethylene (“HDPE”) woven fabric and sacks (“Raffia”). (Source: F&S Report, page 193) In 2024, we ranked among the top global players by revenue, with a 15.4% share of the global woven Raffia machinery market by value. (Source: F&S Report, page 193) We are a market leader in the domestic woven Raffia machines market, with a dominant market share of 40.7% by value in Fiscal 2025. (Source: F&S Report, page 200) As of March 31, 2026, our manufacturing facilities had an installed capacity to produce 240 tapelines, 13,800 circular looms and 108,000 tape winders annually. We manufacture a comprehensive and diverse suite of machinery such as tape extrusion lines, circular loom, coating and lamination lines, printing machines, conversion machines, multifilament yarn machines, twister winders, monofilament extrusion lines and recycling machines, amongst others, as well as spare parts. We provide end-to-end solutions for the entire ecosystem of woven fabric, offering services from ‘concept to commissioning’, throughout the complete production lifecycle required for the Raffia industry. We manufacture winders and rewinders for high performance fibres and we have also ventured into extrusion lines to produce technical monofilaments with diversified applications such as textiles, agriculture and sports. The machines we manufacture enable our customers to deliver solutions across a diverse spectrum of end-user industries, catering to varied applications. Woven fabric machines are used in a wide range of packaging applications across various industries, including the packaging of cement, fertilizer, chemicals, polymer, food grain and minerals, as well as in the production of shopping bags, leno bags, flexible intermediate bulk containers (“FIBC”) and container liners; they are also utilized in a variety of non-packaging applications, such as wrapping fabric, roof underlayment, lumber wrap, pond liner, tarpaulin, geotextile, geogrid, ground cover, carpet backing, ropes and twines. (Source: F&S Report, page 172) Our key product portfolio across core categories are outlined below: The table below sets forth details of the extrusion capacity of manufacturing machinery and equipment sold by us, as of March 31, 2026: Extrusion Capacity of Machinery and Equipment Sold Details of Machinery Domestic Sales Export Sales 8.59 million MT • Over 2,447 tape extrusion lines; • Over 502,940 winders; and • Over 101,452 circular weaving looms 5.80 million MT/ 61.81% 2.79 million MT/ 38.19% The table below sets forth the split of domestic and export sales for the periods indicated: Extrusion Capacity of Machinery and Equipment Sold Fiscal 2026 Fiscal 2025 Fiscal 2024 Domestic Sales Export Sales Domestic Sales Export Sales Domestic Sales Export Sales 61.81% 38.19% 45.30% 54.70% 61.28% 38.72% We own and operate six machine manufacturing facilities, with four in India and one each in USA and Italy, along with one live experience centre in India. Of our Indian manufacturing facilities, two are located in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh along with the live experience centre (where we manufacture FIBCs), and two are located in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Our manufacturing facility in USA is located in Burlington, North Carolina and our manufacturing facility in Italy is located in Como, Italy. For details of the installed capacity of our manufacturing facilities as of March 31, 2026 and the key products manufactured at each facility, see “- Our Competitive Strengths – Advanced manufacturing infrastructure with comprehensive backward integration, supported by an in-house training centre” on page 210. …

Indicatively, globally, the market for woven Raffia machines was estimated to be US$ 1,008 million in 2024, and is expected to reach US$ 1,369 million in 2030, at a CAGR of 5.2%. (Source: F&S Report, page 189) Increasing investments across global infrastructure projects (cement, construction) and increasing usage of Raffia bags across different user segments (food grains, chemicals, fertilizers, agriculture) is expected to support the machinery market growth from 2025 - 2030. (Source: F&S Report, page 189) The Indian market for woven Raffia machines amounted to US$ 150.0 million in Fiscal 2025 and is expected to reach US$ 242.0 million in Fiscal 2030, at a CAGR of 10.0%. (Source: F&S Report, page 196) (Source: F&S Report, page 196) Alongside globally established players like Starlinger & Co. GmbH, our Company holds a leading position in the Raffia machinery industry, ranked among the leading manufacturers worldwide by revenue in 2024. (Source: F&S Report, page 192) Technical textiles are high-performance fabrics engineered for functional applications across industries including automotive, healthcare, construction, and agricultural industries. (Source: F&S Report, page 163). In addition to global growth prospects, in India, the technical textiles market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% between Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2030, from US$ 28.5 billion to US$ 47.0 billion. (Source: F&S Report, page 197) Of this, the Indian woven Raffia market stood at US$ 8.4 billion in Fiscal 2025, with a share of 29.5% of the total technical textile market in India. …

blocks.t: India has one of the youngest populations globally, with a median age of around 28 years. Over 65% of the population is in the working-age group, offering a demographic dividend that can fuel productivity, savings, and consumption over the next two decades. This large, dynamic workforce presents immense potential for innovation, labor-intensive manufacturing, and services-led exports.

India’s urban population is projected to increase from approximately 35% today to over 40% by Fiscal 2030. This shift is creating massive demand for infrastructure, housing, transport, utilities, and digital services. Urbanization also boosts productivity and income through better access to education, healthcare, and job opportunities, enabling a virtuous cycle of growth.

Over the past decade, India has undertaken key structural reforms to enhance economic efficiency and ease of doing business. Initiatives such as GST implementation, Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, Production Linked Incentive (“PLI”) schemes, and liberalized FDI norms have improved transparency, reduced transaction costs, and attracted global capital. Ongoing reforms in land, labor, and digital governance continue to strengthen India’s investment climate. Rise in Per Capita Gross Net Disposable Income With rising incomes and a growing middle class, India’s per capita disposable income is steadily increasing, enhancing purchasing power and shifting consumption patterns. As of Fiscal 2025, nominal GDP per capita is estimated at ₹210,000, with a consistent upward trend projected over the next five years. This income growth fuels higher savings, better living standards, and increased participation in the formal economy. Rise in Private Final Consumption Expenditure ("PFCE") Consumption is the most significant component of India’s GDP, accounting for nearly 60% of total output. PFCE continues to rise, driven by the recovery of rural demand, urban consumption, digital retail expansion, and credit availability. …

India is the second-largest cement producer globally. India’s cement consumption stood at 445 MMT in Fiscal 2024 and is projected to rise to 670 MMT by 2030.Consumption is fueled by infrastructure development, urban housing, rural road projects, and the government’s push under schemes such as PM Awas Yojana, Bharatmala, and the Smart Cities Mission. Growth is expected to continue at a 7 to 8% CAGR, supported by the recovery in construction and real estate.

India consumes over 60 million tonnes of fertilizers annually (including urea, DAP, and MOP). Urea dominates, accounting for approximately 55% of total consumption. Fertilizer demand is seasonal and monsoon-dependent but remains structurally high due to India’s large agricultural base. The government is promoting the balanced application of nutrients, neem-coated urea, and nano-fertilizers to improve efficiency and reduce subsidy costs. The Indian fertilizer market was valued at ₹ 942.1 billion in 2023 and is projected to grow to about ₹ 1,380 billion by 2032, registering a CAGR of approximately 4.2% during 2024 to 2032, driven by rising agricultural demand and sustained government support.

India's chemical consumption spans petrochemicals, agrochemicals, specialty chemicals, and industrial chemicals, with the overall sector valued at US$ 220 billion to US$ 230 billion. Consumption growth is driven by agriculture, textiles, automotive, and FMCG. India is emerging as a global alternative to China in chemical supply chains, with specialty chemicals growing at 10% to 12% CAGR, supported by domestic demand and export potential. Industrial Activity Growth – Increase in IIP Index of Industrial Production (IIP), India, Fiscal 2020 to Fiscal 2025 Source: MOSPI – India, Frost & Sullivan. Between Fiscal 2019 to Fiscal 2020 and Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2025, India's IIP grew at a steady phase, driven by initiatives like the PLI scheme, Make in India, and Atmanirbhar Bharat, which boosted domestic manufacturing and innovation. Key sectors such as automotive, electronics, and pharmaceuticals have thrived on strong consumer demand and export opportunities, highlighting India’s evolving industrial ecosystem and its growing role in global manufacturing and trade. Macro factors like GDP growth, inflation, and landmark policies, along with micro drivers such as skilled labor, infrastructure, and technological advancements, have bolstered industrial activity. …

India’s economy is poised for robust growth in the coming years, supported by rising consumer spending and rapid urbanization. These macroeconomic tailwinds are expected to drive strong demand across a wide range of sectors, including chemicals, pharmaceuticals, food and beverages, and building and construction. This, in turn, will fuel the need for efficient and scalable packaging solutions. Notably, significant capacity expansions in specialty chemicals, industrial chemicals, and petrochemicals are set to open new avenues for growth in the industrial bulk packaging market. Within this space, Flexible Intermediate Bulk Containers (“FIBCs”) account for approximately 60% of the market by unit volume. The FIBC segment is expected to outpace traditional formats such as steel and plastic drums, driven by a clear shift in industry preference toward packaging solutions that offer greater cost efficiency, handling flexibility, and logistical advantages. As industries seek optimized packaging for bulk handling and export operations, FIBCs are increasingly emerging as the preferred choice. Industrial Bulk Packaging Market, India, Revenue Forecast, Fiscal 2019 to Fiscal 2030
Industrial Bulk Packaging Market, India, Volume Forecast, Fiscal 2019 to Fiscal 2030

The Indian industrial bulk packaging market has witnessed steady growth over the past decade and is positioned for substantial expansion through Fiscal 2030. In Fiscal 2019, the market was valued at approximately US$ 470 million, with a volume of around 50 million units. As of Fiscal 2024, the market has grown to an estimated US$ 680 million, driven by increasing demand from the chemical, cement, fertilizer, and food processing industries, as well as rising exports of agricultural and industrial goods. The volume for Fiscal 2024 is estimated at approximately 75 million units. India remains one of the world’s largest producers and exporters of FIBCs, accounting for over 25% of global FIBC export volumes, and continues to strengthen its position in the worldwide packaging supply chain. Looking ahead, the market is expected to expand at a CAGR of 7.8%, reaching US$ 740 million in Fiscal 2025 and crossing US$ 1.15 billion by Fiscal 2030, with volumes likely to reach 120 million units. Increased industrial activity, innovative manufacturing practices, infrastructure push, and the need for safer, certified, and food-grade bulk handling solutions will drive growth. …
